question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that be a static versioned artifact, an authenticated runtime endpoint, or an explicit TypeBox/JSON Schema client-generation path?
rationale: The request defines an external API contract across Gateway methods, auth boundaries, plugin surfaces, and upgrade compatibility, so automation should not choose the schema format or exposure model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning rules, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a release-attached or committed schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime schema endpoint yet.

options.title: Use Existing Protocol Schema Path
options.body: Document the TypeBox/draft-07 JSON Schema pipeline as the intended client-generation surface if maintainers decide OpenAPI is not the right contract.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning rules, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the closest prior OpenAPI/config artifact work and recent Gateway schema history, making him the best first routing candidate for the contract-shape decision.
